notes.title: Open Universal Arabic ASR Leaderboard
notes.bp: An Arabic ASR system should work across dialects rather than appear strong on one convenient corpus.
notes.wh: Dialect, recording, vocabulary, and corpus composition vary together, so a single benchmark can hide generalization failures.
notes.naive: Report one WER on one dialect and treat it as universal Arabic performance.
notes.ap: Build a public multi-dataset leaderboard that compares models across dialects and also exposes robustness, adaptation, efficiency, and memory dimensions.
notes.mech: The benchmark fixes model/data/evaluation axes across six test corpora and records WER plus resource and adaptation measurements.
notes.math: A leaderboard is a measurement design: the set of dialects and denominators determines which kind of generalization is visible.
notes.eval: A leaderboard is a measurement design: the set of dialects and denominators determines which kind of generalization is visible.
notes.ww: The paper reports broad comparative results and identifies differences in dialect robustness, speaker adaptation, inference efficiency, and memory use.
notes.limits: Corpus selection, language variety, transcription conventions, model versions, and leaderboard maintenance bound the conclusion; rankings are not a causal explanation of dialect performance.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Voice Quality Dimensions as Interpretable Primitives for Speaking Style for Atypical Speech and Affect
notes.bp: A speech system needs interpretable estimates of atypical voice qualities such as breathiness, monopitch, or imprecise consonants.
notes.wh: A single embedding score compresses distinct perceptual failures and may not generalize across speakers, elicitation tasks, languages, or disorders.
notes.naive: Train one opaque quality regressor and call its correlation with a rating a complete account of speech accessibility.
notes.ap: Train separate probes for seven voice-quality dimensions on frozen speech representations, then test cross-category and zero-shot transfer.
notes.mech: The frozen representation supplies a common acoustic space while lightweight probes map it to interpretable dimensions; held-out speakers and out-of-domain datasets test transfer.
notes.math: Factorizing a human judgment into named dimensions makes the target inspectable, but each probe still inherits annotation and distribution assumptions.
notes.eval: Factorizing a human judgment into named dimensions makes the target inspectable, but each probe still inherits annotation and distribution assumptions.
notes.ww: The paper reports strong probe performance and generalization on SAP categories, with zero-shot tests on additional languages, tasks, and affect data.
notes.limits: Proxy labels, speaker/sample overlap, limited out-of-domain sets, frozen-encoder choice, and correlation metrics bound transfer; dimensional prediction is not a clinical or listener-outcome validation.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: FlowSE: Efficient and High-Quality Speech Enhancement via Flow Matching
notes.bp: Enhancement should remove noise while retaining the speaker and intelligibility without making real-time use impractical.
notes.wh: Noise removal is a conditional distribution problem: aggressive suppression can erase speech detail, while generative samplers can be slow.
notes.naive: Use a deterministic mask or a many-step diffusion sampler and accept either artifacts or latency.
notes.ap: Use flow matching to learn a continuous transport from noisy to clean speech and combine it with efficient architecture and multi-resolution objectives.
notes.mech: A neural velocity field maps a noisy waveform toward the clean distribution; consistency of the trajectory permits few-step integration while spectral and waveform losses preserve detail.
notes.math: Flow matching replaces repeated stochastic denoising with an ODE-like path whose learned vector field can be sampled in fewer evaluations.
notes.eval: Flow matching replaces repeated stochastic denoising with an ODE-like path whose learned vector field can be sampled in fewer evaluations.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved enhancement quality against generative baselines in both its evaluated scenarios with lower inference cost.
notes.limits: Training data, noise conditions, step count, real-time hardware, perceptual metrics, and speaker preservation tests bound the claim; enhancement scores do not establish conversational benefit.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Calm-Whisper: Reduce Whisper Hallucination On Non-Speech By Calming Crazy Heads Down
notes.bp: An ASR system should remain silent or abstain when the input contains non-speech instead of inventing a transcript.
notes.wh: A sequence decoder is rewarded for plausible language, and non-speech segments lack lexical evidence while still activating learned decoder patterns.
notes.naive: Add a VAD or post-filter around the model and assume the decoder itself has no identifiable source of hallucination.
notes.ap: Diagnose decoder self-attention heads with head-wise masking, identify a small set responsible for most non-speech hallucinations, and fine-tune those heads on non-speech data.
notes.mech: Ablation assigns causal responsibility at the head level; targeted fine-tuning changes the decoder’s response to acoustic absence while monitoring speech WER.
notes.math: The method creates an evidence boundary inside generation: silence should not be converted into a high-probability language continuation.
notes.eval: The method creates an evidence boundary inside generation: silence should not be converted into a high-probability language continuation.
notes.ww: The paper reports that three of twenty decoder heads account for most hallucinations on UrbanSound and that targeted training reduces them with limited LibriSpeech WER degradation.
notes.limits: Non-speech corpus, head attribution, fine-tuning regime, language/model version, and WER tradeoff bound transfer; reduced hallucination is not perfect abstention or factual reliability.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Online Audio-Visual Autoregressive Speaker Extraction
notes.bp: A streaming listener should extract the person being watched even when speakers overlap and attention later switches.
notes.wh: The visual cue is noisy and delayed, the mixture changes over time, and an offline separator can use future context that a live system lacks.
notes.naive: Process each frame independently or optimize only the audio branch while ignoring the extracted signal’s history.
notes.ap: Use a lightweight visual front end and an autoregressive acoustic encoder that feeds past separated speech back into the online model, then test target-switching scenes.
notes.mech: Visual embeddings select the target, while the recurrent acoustic path summarizes prior separated audio; the mask is updated causally under a compute budget.
notes.math: Streaming separation is causal state estimation: the system must preserve target identity while updating its estimate from current visual and acoustic evidence.
notes.eval: Streaming separation is causal state estimation: the system must preserve target identity while updating its estimate from current visual and acoustic evidence.
notes.ww: On LRS3, the paper reports competitive separation quality with about 0.1M visual parameters and 2.1 MACs/s, and evaluates switching attention.
notes.limits: LRS3 faces, switching schedule, audiovisual synchronization, causal latency, and separation metrics bound transfer; benchmark separation is not a full human-attention study.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: RapFlow-TTS: Rapid and High-Fidelity Text-to-Speech with Improved Consistency Flow Matching
notes.bp: A TTS system should produce natural speech quickly enough for interactive use without quality collapsing when sampling steps are reduced.
notes.wh: ODE-based flow generation follows a continuous path but normally needs many numerical steps; shortcutting the path can break consistency and introduce artifacts.
notes.naive: Use a many-step sampler or distill it without constraining the velocity field along the path.
notes.ap: Train RapFlow-TTS with velocity consistency along a straightened flow-matching trajectory, plus time scheduling and adversarial refinement.
notes.mech: The model learns that velocity predictions at different time points agree along the transport path; consistency allows few-step integration while adversarial and acoustic losses protect waveform quality.
notes.math: Consistency regularization turns a generation trajectory into a reusable shortcut: nearby time intervals should imply compatible updates.
notes.eval: Consistency regularization turns a generation trajectory into a reusable shortcut: nearby time intervals should imply compatible updates.
notes.ww: The paper reports high-fidelity synthesis with fewer generation steps than compared flow/diffusion systems.
notes.limits: Text/speaker data, subjective protocol, step counts, vocoder and hardware, and adversarial stability bound the speed-quality claim; fewer steps do not guarantee lower end-to-end latency.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Eigenvoice Synthesis based on Model Editing for Speaker Generation
notes.bp: Generate a plausible unseen speaker voice without requiring a reference utterance from that speaker.
notes.wh: Speaker identity is high-dimensional and entangled with linguistic content; sampling a voice representation can leave the valid speaker manifold.
notes.naive: Interpolate stored speaker embeddings or clone a speaker from a reference sample, which cannot create a genuinely unseen identity without reference audio.
notes.ap: Define an eigenvoice space directly in the parameter space of a DNN TTS model and sample edited model parameters to synthesize new speaker traits.
notes.mech: Model-difference directions act as speaker basis vectors; adding sampled combinations to a base model changes identity while retaining the learned text-to-speech mapping.
notes.math: The speaker manifold can be represented by low-dimensional directions in parameter space rather than only by an input speaker vector.
notes.eval: The speaker manifold can be represented by low-dimensional directions in parameter space rather than only by an input speaker vector.
notes.ww: The paper reports diverse generated voices and compares parameter-space eigenvoice synthesis with prior speaker-generation approaches.
notes.limits: Validity of sampled parameters, diversity and naturalness criteria, speaker-identification protocol, base model, and absence of reference audio bound the claim; generated identity is not evidence of a real person.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Tungnaá In Live Performance: An Implementation Of Interactive Artistic Text-To-Voice
notes.bp: A performer needs text-conditioned voice generation that responds in real time, can be trained from a small bespoke corpus, and remains musically controllable.
notes.wh: Performance demands low worst-case latency and expressive interaction, while ordinary TTS assumes large data, fixed text, and offline generation.
notes.naive: Use a conventional TTS stack and optimize average throughput, even if buffering and model assumptions make live interaction brittle.
notes.ap: Define interactive artistic text-to-voice around a reduced-phonetic-alphabet dataset, streaming vocoder, bounded look-ahead, and a GUI that exposes live controls.
notes.mech: The system separates alignment/generation into streaming components, buffers a small number of frames to trade latency for stability, and keeps the interface in a separate process.
notes.math: Deployment constraints become part of the speech representation and evaluation: latency, controllability, and small-data adaptation matter alongside audio quality.
notes.eval: Deployment constraints become part of the speech representation and evaluation: latency, controllability, and small-data adaptation matter alongside audio quality.
notes.ww: The demonstration reports real-time inference with worst-case latency below 100 ms and a bespoke performance dataset/application.
notes.limits: Demonstration scope, artist-specific data, reduced phonetic alphabet, hardware, subjective quality, and no controlled comparison bound generalization; live usability is not a standard TTS benchmark.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.
